I was pleased to welcome three new players this past Saturday to the league. Our group is still quite small, so we had just two regular games before I showed up as the sixth person, and then we decided to break from the normal plan and actually run a 3 vs 3 game. 

 

The volcano played a _huge_ role in that game. Blade, after being pumped up by Legacy, charged across the board to the lip of the volcano in order to one-shot Omnitron with a Fission Blast, but Omnitron stood up the next turn and dragged Blade through the lava, incapacitating him back. Ambuscade set off a stack of traps that caught both Dawn and Legacy. Dawn and Legacy had their chances for retribution, but made poor choices, in retrospect about whether or not to aim.

 

Updated stats: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rS3MH6bRVsU_2KL80f6kqUxyj78UNen45gPo_C2Mc-o/edit?usp=sharing

posts.cooked:
Only three of us yesterday , but we had a great time.

With just three of us, we decided to focus on checking out the playtest characters rather than doing ban/draft games. Dylan had brought maps from the GenCon 2015 Tactics tournament. Bharyn had his awesome buildings. I'd brought my dice trays. We had the playtest characters that Russ printed and prepped. It was great!

It was a bit odd working out how to have three of us playing a single game. We settled on Ian controlling a side of three characters and Dylan and I on the other team with Dylan controlling two and me controlling one. Then, for our second game Ian and I switched places, so, we played two games and collectively managed four characters each. 

I'm not sure if I enjoyed it more in the game where I controlled one character or the game where I controlled three! Controlling all three characters oneself is a really great way to come up with tactics that involve multiple characters, but it's a lot to juggle at once, particularly when playing new characters, and particularly with the three I was managing.

 

After Ian took off, Dylan and I had time for another game. Dylan was keen to play a scenario and I couldn't resist the siren call of getting to see the Underboss minis in play, so we played the Operative scenario. I had the advantage, having played it once before, and was able to lead my thugs to victory, despite three of my Underbosses being incapacitated.

 

We discussed a little bit the future of the league. Obviously, interest is low, but Ian and I agreed that as long as we were enjoying getting together to play there was no reason to stop. We also talked about what we might do for Who's Yer Con. More about that in its own thread.
